title: 7 Power Prompts to Get Better Answers From Claude
description:
Same AI, very different answers. The difference is how you ask. In this lesson you'll learn 7 simple power prompts that get clearer, more useful answers from Claude, with real examples you can copy: explain it at your level, give it a role, let it ask you questions, show an example, set the format, go step by step, and critique and improve.

Features change over time, so check claude.ai for the latest.

🔔 Subscribe to Learn AI with MHR for new AI lessons every day.

Not affiliated with Anthropic.

#claude #ai #prompts #learnai #claudeai

scenes.narration: Same AI. Same question. Completely different answers. The difference? How you ask.
In this lesson, you'll learn seven power prompts that get clearer, more useful answers from Claude. Every one comes with an example you can copy.
Most people type a few words and hope for the best. Power users tell Claude exactly what they need.

visual.title: Guessing vs *guiding*
items: Most people: A few words and hope

scenes.narration: Power prompt number one. Explain it at my level.
Claude can explain anything, from beginner to expert. So tell it your level. Like: explain how the stock market works like I'm a complete beginner.

visual.title: Set your level
items: Explain how the stock market works like I'm a complete beginner.
Think of a company as a pizza cut into slices. Each slice is a share. When you buy a share, you own a tiny piece of the company, and its value goes up or down with how the company does.

scenes.narration: You can say like I'm ten, like I'm a beginner, or like I'm an expert. Same topic, totally different depth.
Power prompt number two. Give it a role.
Tell Claude who to be, and it changes the style and focus of the answer. For example: act as a friendly career coach and review my plan to switch jobs.

visual.title: Assign a role
items: Act as a friendly career coach. I want to switch from retail to marketing. Where do I start?
Great goal! Start with your strengths: retail teaches you how customers think. Next, take a free intro marketing course, then build two small sample projects to show employers.

scenes.narration: Try a patient tutor, a strict editor, a personal trainer, or a travel planner. The role tells Claude what kind of help you want.
Power prompt number three. This one is a game changer. Let Claude ask you questions first.
Instead of guessing what you need, Claude can interview you. Just add: before you answer, ask me three questions.

visual.title: Questions first
items: Help me plan a birthday party. Before you answer, ask me 3 questions.
Happy to help! 1. Who is the party for, and how old are they? 2. Roughly how many guests and what's your budget? 3. Do you prefer home, a venue, or outdoors?

scenes.narration: You answer, and the final result fits you perfectly. It's like working with someone who actually listens.
Power prompt number four. Show an example.
Describing a style is hard. Showing it is easy. Paste an example of what you like, and ask Claude to match it.

visual.title: Tell vs *show*
items: Tell: Write it in a fun tone
Show: Here's one I like, match this style

scenes.narration: For example: here's a product description I love. Write one in the same style for my handmade candles.

visual.title: Match my style
items: Here's a description I love: 'Soft, warm, and made to slow your evening down.' Write one like it for my handmade candles.
Hand-poured, gently scented, and made to turn any quiet night into your favourite part of the day.

scenes.narration: Power prompt number five. Set the format.

visual.title: Set the format
visual.subtitle: Get it the way you want

scenes.narration: Tell Claude exactly how you want the answer to look. A table. Bullet points. An email. Or a word limit.
For example: compare three budget laptops for students in a table with price range, battery life, and best use.

visual.title: Ask for a table
items: Compare 3 types of budget laptop for students in a table: price range, battery life, best use.
Here's a simple table comparing a Chromebook, a budget Windows laptop and an entry-level MacBook, with typical price range, battery life and what each is best for.

scenes.narration: Power prompt number six. Go step by step.
For anything tricky, like a math problem, a plan, or a decision, ask Claude to walk you through it step by step. You'll understand the answer, not just get it.

visual.title: Walk me through it
items: Walk me through how to calculate a 15% tip on $48, step by step.
Step 1: 10% of $48 is $4.80. Step 2: 5% is half of that, $2.40. Step 3: add them together. $4.80 plus $2.40 equals $7.20.

scenes.narration: This works brilliantly for learning. Instead of copying an answer, you see the thinking behind it.

visual.title: *Learn* the why
visual.subtitle: See the thinking, not just the answer

scenes.narration: And power prompt number seven. Critique and improve.
Paste anything you've written, and ask Claude to find the weak spots first, then improve it. Like: here's my cover letter, what are its three biggest weaknesses, then rewrite it.

visual.title: Find the weak spots
visual.subtitle: cover_letter.docx
items: What are the 3 biggest weaknesses in my cover letter? Then rewrite it.
1. The opening is generic. 2. It lists duties instead of results. 3. It doesn't say why you want this company. Here's a stronger version that fixes all three.

scenes.narration: Asking for the weaknesses first makes the improvements smarter, because Claude explains what's wrong before fixing it.
Now here's the real secret. Combine them. Use a role, your level, and a format in one prompt.

visual.title: *Combine* them
visual.subtitle: Role + level + format in one prompt

scenes.narration: Like this. Act as a patient tutor. Explain photosynthesis like I'm a beginner, in five short bullet points.

visual.title: All together
items: Act as a patient tutor. Explain photosynthesis like I'm a beginner, in 5 short bullet points.
Plants make their own food. They use sunlight as energy. They take in water and carbon dioxide. They turn these into sugar. And they release oxygen, the air we breathe.

scenes.narration: And remember, even with great prompts, always double-check important facts. Better prompts mean better answers, but you're still in charge.
Let's recap the seven power prompts. Explain at my level. Give it a role. Let it ask you. Show an example.
Set the format. Go step by step. And critique and improve.
Pick one and try it today. Then subscribe, because next lesson, we'll use Claude with your own files: PDFs, notes, and images.
